name: NC-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+24 partisan lean gives Democrats a floor no plausible swing approaches
Alma Adams is an entrenched incumbent with a $456k cash advantage
Republican Jack Codiga has raised under $29k and has essentially no cash on hand
No public polling in the race, so the exact margin carries wide uncertainty
model.rationale: The seat sits in a D+24 Charlotte-area district, and Adams holds every practical advantage: incumbency, a six-figure war chest against a rival reporting $3 on hand, and no outside money working against her. Markets price her near-certain, and the only real unknown is the size of the margin, not the winner.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary development, such as a major scandal or a flood of late outside spending for Codiga, would matter, and even that would likely move the margin more than the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Carolina's 12th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of D+24, and Rep. Alma Adams has held it comfortably since 2014. She is running for renomination and enters the general election with a substantial financial edge, reporting roughly $456,000 on hand after raising about $370,000 this cycle.

Republican Jack Codiga has raised under $29,000 and reports just $3 in cash, with no outside spending on either side, leaving him little visible infrastructure to contest the seat. Prediction markets price Adams' chances at roughly 96 percent or better, and no public polling contradicts that picture. The forecast calls the race Safe Democratic, with Adams expected to win by roughly 26 points; the main uncertainty is turnout in a low-profile contest, not the winner.
